title: A stand-in for a linter

blocks.md:
## Refuse `==` in the edit file

LAWP’s `ast` check is a **substring** search, not a real parser pass. Treat it as a stand-in for a linter. The file text must contain `===` and must not use `==`.

`same(a, b)` compares with `===`. Print `false` for `0` and `""` — those are different kinds.

The desk once filed `0` (lamp off) as the same as a missing name `""` because someone wrote `==`. The fox route test uses `===` so off and missing stay different.

choices.md: A stand-in: the file text must not use `==`

blocks.promptMd: This lesson runs a full ESLint pass on your file.
blocks.explainMd: The grader looks for === in the file text and rejects ==. That is a stand-in, not ESLint.

hintLadder.md: `==` would treat `0` and `""` as the same. This lesson refuses that.

description: A linter reads the shape of the code, not only the text.
